item.title: Strengthening the Party
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Strengthening the Party Plenum: Guiding principles highlighted A key meeting of the Communist Party of China, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing, adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, highlighting that the significance of strengthening the Party must be understood from the strategic height of consolidating the Party's long-term governance and realizing national rejuvenation. The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presided over the four-day fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, at which Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, said a communique issued after the meeting. The CPC Central Committee decided at the plenum that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027, the communique said. At the session, participants heard and discussed a report on the work of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presented by Xi. They also considered and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Xi delivered explanatory remarks on the draft of the resolution. The CPC Central Committee spoke highly of the great achievements that the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era, saying that deep-seated problems that had plagued the Party for years have been remedied, and serious dangers hidden within the Party, the State and the military have been removed. The Party has found two answers to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall: the people's oversight over government and the Party's self-reform, the communique said, adding that these are the unique discoveries of the CPC, and will forever stand out in the history of Marxist parties. It was emphasized at the session that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor remain, the communique said. Profound changes in global, national and Party conditions have made even more arduous the Party's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity, according to the communique. The session emphasized the need to uphold the Party's overall leadership and the centralized and unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee, with a focus on enhancing the Party's capacity for long-term governance, preserving its advanced nature and integrity, and maintaining its close bond with the people. It urged improving the system of full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the Party always remains a vibrant Marxist governing party that stays at the forefront of the times, enjoys the wholehearted support of the people, and is able to withstand all tests, and that it always remains the strong leadership core of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the communique said. At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking the strengthening of the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations. Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were made at the session, including improving conduct and tightening discipline on an ongoing basis, taking firm and coordinated action against corruption, running the Party with systems and regulations, and refining Party and State oversight systems, according to the communique. It was noted at the session that strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, urging the application of stringent standards to the education, cultivation, selection, appointment, management and oversight of officials, in order to build up the lineup of high-caliber officials with firm political commitment, outstanding professional competence, excellent work conduct and strict discipline, the communique said. The session highlighted taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity or desire to commit corruption. It was also noted that strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance. "Stronger measures will be taken to improve the framework of Party regulations and institutions, ensure the enforcement of institutions and eliminate hidden rules," the communique said. At the session, Zhang Shengmin, vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission, was elected a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. The session also decided on the filling of empty seats on the CPC Central Committee by alternate members, deliberated and adopted inspection reports of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Central Military Commission on those committing grave violations of discipline and laws, and confirmed the Political Bureau's previous decisions to punish those violators.

item.title: 1st cross-border tourism zone scores big
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
1st cross-border tourism zone scores big The China-Vietnam Detian-Ban Gioc Waterfall cross-border tourism cooperation zone, China's first of its kind, has achieved key successes since its official launch, as tourist arrivals surged in the first three quarters, fueled by pioneering smart clearance measures. Located in the Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, the cooperation zone has transformed the regional tourism landscape. Xu Yu, deputy director of the service center at the scenic area in Daxin county of Chongzuo, noted that the zone has maintained a flawless record of zero errors and zero incidents since its trial operation in September 2023, handling nearly 160,000 inbound and outbound visits. To ensure smooth operations, local authorities have established a normalized communication mechanism with Vietnam, advancing joint management and the construction of the No 53 old boundary marker cultural square to build a benchmark for high-standard opening-up, Xu added. The operational shift has brought unprecedented convenience to visitors, allowing them to explore destinations in both countries within a single day. Long Shengwang, director of the cross-border tourism management department at CTS Detian Waterfall Tourism Development Co, explained that the scenic area has transitioned from a single-destination operation to a comprehensive cross-border experience. "We established a dedicated department and pioneered an integrated ticketing approach that covers attractions on both sides of the border by pooling bilateral resources," Long said. Tourists can complete bookings in advance by linking the scenic area's platform with the immigration department's mini-program, enjoying one-stop services at a centralized hall. To handle large tourist flows, the company coordinates with multiple government departments to form a closed-loop safety management system, ensuring visitors experience comprehensive services domestically and appropriate guidance abroad. This seamless experience is heavily supported by innovative customs procedures, notably the national debut of facial recognition-based permit processing. Hu Manyin, deputy commissioner of Shuolong Customs, highlighted the creation of a customized clearance model tailored for tour groups. "We implemented advance luggage declarations and centralized inspections, optimizing procedures for camera equipment to meet tourists' sightseeing needs," Hu said. Utilizing non-intrusive equipment like infrared thermometers and X-ray machines, customs authorities established a contactless inspection system, enabling travelers to pass through within 20 seconds. According to Hu, the zone welcomed 54,450 tourists from January to September, a 40.4 percent year-on-year increase, with a record single-day high of 1,272 visitors. "Efficient clearance not only fulfills our duty to safeguard the border and promote development but also injects strong momentum into the local economy," Hu added. Enhancing the humanistic aspect of border management, the Detian Women Police Vanguard of the Shuolong Border Defense Station provides crucial support. Police officer Zhang Weihuayu stated that the station has provided over 5,000 consultation services. "Facing frequent foreign exchanges, our female officers utilize a meticulous and gentle approach to improve the clearance experience," Zhang said. To maximize convenience, border inspection rolled out measures such as exempting foreign tourists from fingerprint collection, passport stamping and filling out entry cards, facilitating a more welcoming environment for international visitors. Beyond tourism, the cooperation zone serves as a vital platform for cultural exchange and rural vitalization. According to Long, to further tap into the broader Association of Southeast Asian Nations market, the scenic area has launched targeted promotional campaigns in countries like Vietnam and Thailand, inviting foreign media for on-site reporting. Innovative programs, such as cross-border youth hiking exchanges and water-based folk song gatherings, have also been introduced to diversify the tourism portfolio. These frequent bilateral events attracted over 100,000 participants in 2026 alone, significantly strengthening ties between the people of both nations. Xu noted that this booming cross-border tourism directly drives surrounding sectors, such as accommodation, catering and cultural products. The influx of visitors during peak seasons and traditional holidays, such as the regional March 3 Festival — an important traditional event for ethnic minorities in Guangxi — has stimulated local businesses. By promoting intangible cultural heritage displays and specialty agricultural products, the zone encourages the development of rural enterprises. Expanding consumption scenarios through departure tax refund shops, among others, enables border residents to find employment and increase their incomes, effectively boosting the regional economy, Xu said. renqi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: At least 68 killed in Spain train collision
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
At least 68 killed in high-speed train collision in Spain Rescue crews and crash investigators were combing through the wreckage on Wednesday after two high-speed trains collided near Toledo in central Spain. At least 68 people were killed in the accident, authorities said. The crash involved a passenger train operated by Spain's state-owned national railway company Renfe, and one operated by the country's first private high-speed rail company, Iryo. The collision shortly after 9 am local time caused several carriages from the Iryo train to fully derail, according to a government spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha autonomous region, where the accident happened. The official added that the cause and the final death toll were not immediately known. The number of confirmed deaths from the train crash has reached 68, Castilla-La Mancha's regional government said on Wednesday. A spokesperson for ADIF, the state-owned company that manages Spain's railway infrastructure, said the incident happened between the towns of Mora and Orgaz, and that the trains were both traveling from Madrid to Seville when one slammed into the other train while it was stationary. ADIF added in a message on X: "Traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line has been suspended following a rear-end collision between two trains." Iryo said it had also triggered "all emergency protocols" to ascertain what happened. "This morning, our train 6076, traveling from Madrid to Seville, was involved in an accident near Urda, at kilometer point 118," the company said, adding it was "working closely with the relevant authorities to manage the situation". It added that all services from Madrid's Atocha station bound for Spain's south had been canceled, and that "at this time, there is no estimate for when service will be restored". The Independent newspaper quoted Manuel Galan, the mayor of Urda, the small municipality where the accident happened, as saying the emergency services had asked him to make a sports hall available to accommodate injured passengers and to mount a triage operation. The Spanish newspaper El Pais quoted federal coordinator Antonio Maillo as saying he feared for "the worst" after the "very serious accident" and that the death toll was likely to rise. The Renfe train had 397 passengers on board at the time, while the Iryo train had 147. The Chinese embassy in Spain has confirmed that four Chinese nationals were aboard the trains involved in the collision, with at least one sustaining minor injuries. Political parties across Spain canceled scheduled activities on Wednesday, while officials expressed their condolences for those affected. Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was "shocked by the serious train accident" and was in constant contact with his transport minister and other relevant authorities. A spokesperson for Spain's emergency services told Agence France-Presse shortly after the collision that "all resources" were being deployed, including "several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units". Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia said in a short statement on X that they were following news of the accident. "We are deeply saddened and concerned by the train accident in Urda (Toledo)," the royal couple said. "We share in the grief of the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, and we send our heartfelt support to the injured and all those affected." The crash was the latest in a series of tragic accidents that have plagued Spain's railway system. In January, a high-speed train derailed in southern Spain into the path of an oncoming Renfe train, resulting in 46 deaths. Xinhua and agencies contributed to this story.

item.title: China expands foreign business access at Hainan FTP
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
China expands foreign business access at world's largest free trade port BEIJING -- China has unveiled 16 measures to make it easier for foreign businesses and professionals to operate in the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP), the world's largest FTP by area, with new policies covering energy trade, medical services and bonded business operations, according to a government circular made public Thursday. Under the measures, foreign physicians legally licensed to practice medicine overseas may obtain permits to provide clinical diagnosis and treatment services in Hainan for up to three years, with extensions available in accordance with relevant regulations. More convenient policies regarding work permits and stay and residence will also be introduced for foreign nationals. The Hainan FTP, located in China's southernmost island province, launched island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, allowing freer entry of overseas goods, expanded zero-tariff coverage and more business-friendly measures as part of China's efforts to promote high-standard opening-up. Overseas companies will be allowed to use bonded facilities at Hainan's liquefied natural gas (LNG) receiving terminals, while the FTP will be supported in conducting LNG futures delivery warehouse operations after LNG futures contracts are launched. Other measures include promoting offshore trade, expanding the range of products eligible for bonded maintenance, facilitating the entry of eligible bonded remanufactured products into pilot free trade zones on the Chinese mainland, encouraging the use of the yuan in new forms of barter trade, and deepening the FTP's economic and trade cooperation with China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The circular was jointly issued by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the General Administration of Customs.

item.title: Vice-minister Liao's name proposed for IMF role
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
Vice-minister Liao's name proposed for IMF role The expected succession of International Monetary Fund Deputy Managing Director Li Bo by a veteran Chinese fiscal policymaker would maintain continuity in China's representation, experts said. This could also offer an additional perspective on the fund's work on sovereign debt restructuring and macroeconomic policy coordination, they added. Liao Min, China's vice-minister of finance, will bring experience across financial regulation, fiscal policymaking and international consultations that could help economies to better balance their respective domestic policy priorities with the need for multilateral cooperation, they said. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said in a statement published on the fund's website on Wednesday that she had proposed Liao to succeed Li as deputy managing director. Li's term ends on Nov 30. The proposed appointment would take effect on Dec 1. Georgieva noted Liao's more than three decades of experience in banking, financial regulation and macroeconomic governance. "He has been deeply engaged in global macropolicy coordination and in bilateral and multilateral fiscal, financial and trade cooperation. His experience at the intersection of domestic reform and international economic cooperation will be a tremendous asset to the fund and our membership," she said. Since 2011, three Chinese nationals — Zhu Min, Zhang Tao and Li Bo — have successively held the IMF deputy managing director's position. All three had previously served as deputy governors of the People's Bank of China. Liao has served as vice-minister of finance since 2018, after earlier roles in central banking and financial regulation. The proposed appointment suggests that, alongside maintaining China's representation, the IMF is placing greater emphasis on aligning leadership expertise with its evolving priorities, said Dong Ximiao, chief economist at Merchants Union Consumer Finance and executive director of the Shanghai Institution for Finance and Development. As fiscal sustainability, sovereign debt restructuring and fiscal-monetary policy coordination draw more attention, Dong said that Liao's understanding of domestic policy constraints could help facilitate debt restructuring discussions and support dialogue during the IMF's country surveillance process. At the second G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting of 2026, Liao said that with the global economy facing multiple challenges, the G20 should further practice true multilateralism, strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and work toward stronger global growth. He also urged members to uphold free trade, promote universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and create a favorable policy environment for international trade and capital flows. Liao's experience in the G20's finance discussions and bilateral fiscal and financial consultations could help turn expectations into practical cooperation, said Tian Lihui, a finance professor at Nankai University in Tianjin. His engagement in international fiscal and financial consultations could help bridge policy differences and facilitate dialogue among debtor countries, creditors and international institutions, Tian said. item.title: Tianjin's Xibeijiao serves up a taste of local life
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
In Tianjin's Xibeijiao neighborhood, getting breakfast can be an early-morning test of patience. Xibeijiao's eateries attract crowds well before much of the city is fully awake, and by midmorning, finding a place to sit down can be a challenge. For those who make it early, the reward is a hearty breakfast and a glimpse of the city starting its day. Steam rises from baskets of buns, pancakes sizzle on hot griddles and freshly fried snacks emerge from busy kitchens. Customers line up at familiar stalls, pick up breakfast to go or pause to eat before heading off to work. The experience offers a different way to discover Tianjin, a port city in northern China better known to many visitors for its European-style architecture, historical streets and riverfront. Lin Yaqi, a visitor from Singapore, made a special trip to the neighborhood with her friends in mid-October after seeing enthusiastic recommendations online. They tasted jianbing guozi, steamed buns and snacks they had never tried before. "There were so many choices," Lin recalled. "You walk just a few steps and there's another shop, and everything smelled so good!" She was particularly taken with jianbing guozi, a Tianjin breakfast staple made by spreading mung bean batter on a hot griddle, cracking an egg onto the pancake and folding it around a fried dough stick or a crispy cracker, with sauces added for extra flavor. The appeal lies partly in the combination of textures — the thin, tender pancake, the crispness of the filling and the savory sauces. Prepared fresh to order, it is easy to eat on the way to work, yet substantial enough to keep hunger at bay through the morning. For Lin, having breakfast like a local offered a glimpse of Tianjin beyond its tourist attractions and a way to understand the city through the daily routines of its residents. The mix of food and daily life is what defines Xibeijiao, a historical breakfast hub in Lingdangge subdistrict in Tianjin's Hongqiao district, where food businesses sit alongside homes and neighborhood services. Liu Tao, a senior official of Lingdangge subdistrict, noted that Xibeijiao brings together residential life, commerce and tourism. Many food businesses have been passed down through generations, while the neighborhood's character also reflects the history and food traditions of its Hui ethnic community, he said. Tianjin's history as a trading and transportation hub helps to explain the place of hearty, convenient meals in its food culture. Goods moved through the city along the Grand Canal and its waterways, while workers engaged in loading and transporting goods needed food to sustain long working days. In Xibeijiao, generations of local families helped turn the preparation and sale of traditional snacks into an enduring part of community life. Xu Peng's grandmother began selling jianbing guozi in Tianjin's old Nanshi area in 1958. Xu grew up watching her make the pancakes, and the family opened its shop in Xibeijiao in 2024. For Xu, the appeal of the traditional Tianjin pancake lies in its simplicity. The fillings are basic, and that allows all the flavors to come through. "Too many additions can overwhelm the original taste," he said. The shop serves regular customers as well as visitors curious about how the breakfast staple is made. Its open kitchen lets customers try preparing their own jianbing guozi, turning a quick meal into a hands-on experience. The family has also created themed plush toys as souvenirs, giving visitors a playful reminder of a dish that local residents eat without a second thought. For Xu, introducing visitors to jianbing guozi is also a way of introducing them to the city that gave the dish its character. "We have a responsibility to let visitors to Tianjin experience not only the food, but also the city's local culture, customs and everyday life," he said.

item.title: Australia returns ancient relics to China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
Australia handed over to China two Northern Song Dynasty (960-1127) head statues in a major ceremony on Wednesday, the latest repatriation of Chinese relics under joint efforts to protect cultural heritage and build on ties between the two nations. At the National Gallery of Australia in Canberra, senior officials and representatives from both sides witnessed the handover of the head statues of a civil official and a military official, from the Song imperial mausoleums in Gongyi, Central China's Henan province, near the then-capital of Kaifeng. Speaking at the ceremony, Chinese Ambassador to Australia Liu Jinsong said the two statues "once stood quietly guarding the ancient tombs. They have seen the passage of time and traveled across the oceans". According to the National Gallery of Australia, the relics became part of its collection in 1995. China's National Cultural Heritage Administration said in a statement that the restitution process of the statues was initiated with a request to the National Gallery of Australia in 2025 to return them, following investigations and studies by relevant Chinese authorities. The two sides subsequently worked together under international conventions and agreements on the protection of cultural property, and successfully secured the return of the relics to China. The ambassador expressed his heartfelt appreciation to "all the Australian institutions and individuals who have contributed to this return", and thanked the museum and heritage professionals from both countries for their work. "The return of these two statues is not the end of their story. It is a new beginning for research, conservation and cultural heritage," he said. Nick Mitzevich, director of the National Gallery of Australia, said it is committed to the "ethical management of the national collection through due diligence and proactive provenance research". "We value and respect international collaboration and we consider repatriation to be more than a physical return of an object. It is an act of respect, an act of responsibility and an act of world partnership," he said. Tang Wei, deputy director of China's National Cultural Heritage Administration, said that promoting the return of cultural objects lost overseas to their countries of origin is "an act of justice", safeguarding cultural heritage and the "national sentiments of people". He said that government agencies, museums and cultural heritage institutions in China and Australia have worked closely in recent years to honor their commitment to the protection of cultural heritage under international frameworks. The repatriation of the Song statues comes three years after Australia returned five relics to China, including two figurines dating back about 1,400 years ago, and a reptile fossil from northeastern China dating back to between 133 and 120 million years ago. Duan Yong, director of the Center for Research on Chinese Cultural Relics Abroad at Shanghai University, said that over the past decade, the recovery and return of lost cultural relics have shown "a trend that is relatively favorable to countries, including China, that suffered the loss of their cultural heritage". He explained that countries dispossessed of their cultural heritage have continued to make recovery efforts to protect their cultural rights and interests. The spirit of relevant international conventions — such as UNESCO's 1970 Convention and the UNIDROIT 1995 Convention — is gaining wider acceptance, providing an important legal basis for recovery and return. "In the recovery of lost cultural relics, research on provenance and transfer history is very important and plays a decisive role, especially in litigation," he said. "The return of cultural relics by the Australian side was precisely due to sufficient provenance." He called for strengthening research on the provenance and transfer history of lost cultural relics, enhancing registration and filing for relics in domestic collections and private hands, and conducting thorough exploration and investigation of buried relics. Contact the writers at xinxin@chinadaily.com.cn XIN XIN and ALEXIS HOOI in Canberra and DENG ZHANGYU in Beijing

item.title: 'Super students' ride tide of AI innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
'Super students' ride tide of AI innovation School-age creators developing tools, programs to solve real-world problems At just 14, Zhang Shaoqing's prowess with AI tools means he could easily be included in the ranks of the new wave of "super students" but it's a description he balks at. "Daring to imagine and daring to try is encouraging, but it's also a kind of pressure; it's as if I'm not a good student unless I've built something," said the ninth-grader at Wuxi Dipont School of Arts and Science in Jiangsu province. "I don't want to be defined as a 'super student.' I would rather be seen as an ordinary student who has stayed passionate about one field for a long time," he added. His mother Liu Liwei, who has encouraged his development and interests, is also uncomfortable with the super student label, which has recently gained online traction. Many youngsters involved in sophisticated technology projects are not necessarily way ahead of others, but have benefited from opportunities, guidance and supportive environments, she said. "I always remind him not to think he is better than others. He has simply received opportunities that many students may not have had," said Liu. From developing artificial intelligence tools for schools to creating digital content, a growing number of Chinese teenagers are moving from technology users to creators, offering a glimpse into how they are exploring opportunities and challenges in the AI era. In recent years, Chinese school students have begun participating in AI competitions, open-source communities and industry-linked innovation programs once mainly associated with university students and professionals. Tencent Youth Tech Training Camp, launched in 2016, has attracted more than 900,000 users to its platform, partnered with over 2,000 schools and accumulated more than 40,000 works as of September 2026. Dong Xinye, deputy director of the Youth Innovation Education Center at Shenzhen InnoX Academy, an education program that aims to nurture innovative talent for the AI era through project-based learning, said teenagers' participation in AI and innovation programs has grown significantly in recent years. "What was once a niche interest among a small number of technology enthusiasts has gradually become a mainstream way for young people to explore the world," said Dong.

item.title: Unity key to greater voice of Global South
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Unity key to greater voice of Global South Global South nations should build on their unity and amplify their voice in multilateral mechanisms to better enjoy the dividends of evolving technologies and economic globalization, prominent political figures, scholars and media executives said on Wednesday. They made the remarks at the Global Strategic Dialogue (2026), a high-end think tank forum held in Beijing. Themed "Unite Global South, Improve Global Governance", the forum was hosted by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and China Daily. It gathered over 100 leading researchers and experts from countries including China, Russia, France and Austria. Li Xuesong, vice-president of the CASS, noted that China will host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, in November and assume the presidency of BRICS next year. By seizing these opportunities, "China will work with various parties to forge consensus, expand cooperation and advocate an equal and orderly multipolar world and inclusive economic globalization", Li said at the opening of the forum. For global governance, countries should lay a solid foundation through genuine multilateralism, boost quality and efficiency through sustainable and shared development, and fix setbacks through innovative cooperation mechanisms, he said. Li called for more efforts to oppose politicization and weaponization of economic and trade issues, and "create favorable conditions for Global South countries to integrate into the international division of labor and cooperation and share dividends of economic globalization". Djoomart Otorbaev, former prime minister of Kyrgyzstan, said that efforts to reform the international system and global governance remain inadequate, and that the Global South should be fairly and appropriately represented in global governance structures. Regarding the shareholder structure and voting rights of the International Monetary Fund, he said, "Why don't we give the countries of the Global South more voting rights?" It was remarkable that during the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization Plus" Meeting in September 2025, President Xi Jinping proposed the Global Governance Initiative "not to replace the existing (international) system, but to reform it to reflect our world order", Otorbaev said. Technologies such as artificial intelligence "are evolving faster than our capacity to govern", he said, adding that "the world is simply changing much faster than the structures meant to guide it". Xing Zhigang, deputy editor-in-chief of China Daily, said that as key players in knowledge production, policy coordination and discourse shaping, think tanks in the Global South play an irreplaceable role in building collective consensus and optimizing international rules. "The Global South should build on consensus, speak with one voice, and constantly boost its drive to set international agendas," he said. Think tanks in the Global South should provide evidence-based policy analysis and research, participate in the process of optimizing international rules, and foster the creation of original perspectives while building an independent discourse system, Xing said. They should also support multilateral practices, bridge the gap between concepts and institutional implementation, establish platforms for dialogue and foster consensus, he added. Zou Jiayi, president and chair of the board of directors of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, said the Global South can contribute to reshaping development cooperation. More developing countries are becoming active shareholders and donors of multilateral development banks, and emerging and developing economies are important driving forces behind economic transformation, she said. Zou said that she visited more than 30 member economies of the AIIB — most of them developing economies — over the past few months, and was encouraged by the consistent message calling for more infrastructure and infrastructure financing. "Emerging and developing economies play a pivotal role in rebalancing the global economy. When trade protectionism is pervasive in some parts of the world, most developing economies continue to embrace openness in trade and investment," she said.
